stem.text: Find the interval of convergence of the power series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{3 \left(x - 1\right)^{n}}{5^{n} n^{2}} \). Use the ratio test for the interior and justify the behaviour at each endpoint.

answer_key.label: The interval of convergence is \( -4 \le x \le 6 \).

worked_solution.text: For the ratio test, form \( \left|\frac{\frac{3 \left(x - 1\right)^{n+1}}{5^{n+1} (n+1)^{2}}}{\frac{3 \left(x - 1\right)^{n}}{5^{n} n^{2}}}\right| \).
The series converges when \( \frac{\left|x - 1\right|}{5} < 1 \), that is \( \left|x - 1\right| < 5 \), so \( -4 < x < 6 \).

At \( x = 6 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{3}{n^{2}} \), which converges by the p-series test, since it is a multiple of a p-series with \( p = 2 > 1 \). At \( x = -4 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{3 (-1)^n}{n^{2}} \), which converges by the alternating series test, since its terms alternate and their sizes decrease to 0.
The interval of convergence is \( -4 \le x \le 6 \).

options.label: The interval of convergence is \( -4 \le x < 6 \).
options.derivation: the endpoint where the series is a positive p-series excluded, although the p-series test showed it converges

options.label: The interval of convergence is \( x \le 6 \).
options.derivation: the absolute value dropped when solving, so x - 1 < 5 was kept as the whole solution and only the endpoint 6 tested
